t: #3455 Shortest Matching Substring — Split on Stars + KMP
o: The pattern is A*B*C. A matching substring must contain a match of A ending before a match of B, which ends before a match of C, and its length is (end of C) − (start of A). To minimize it, for a fixed occurrence of B spanning [x, y) we want the latest possible start of an A ending at or before x, and the earliest possible end of a C starting at or after y. Empty parts match everywhere, which neatly handles patterns like "**" (answer 0) and boundary cases.
k: Any part may be empty; an empty part matches at every position.
Precompute latestA[e] = latest start of an A-match ending at e (prefix max), earliestC[s] = earliest end of a C-match starting at s (suffix min).
Answer = min over B-occurrences [x,y) of earliestC[y] − latestA[x].
KMP finds all occurrences in linear time, avoiding quadratic blowups on periodic strings.

a.i: Run KMP once per non-empty part to get occurrence lists. Fold A-occurrences into a prefix-max array of start positions indexed by end position, and C-occurrences into a suffix-min array of end positions indexed by start position. Initialize with the identity (empty part matches at each cut) so all degenerate cases fall out automatically. Scan B-occurrences (or all cut points if B is empty) and combine.
s: Split p on the two '*' into a, b, c.
KMP each non-empty part; fill latestA (prefix max) and earliestC (suffix min), seeding empties with the identity.
For each B span [x, y), update the answer with earliestC[y] − latestA[x] when both sides exist.
Return the minimum, or -1 if never updated.
a.t: O(n + |p|) — three KMP runs plus linear folds and scans
a.sp: O(n) — occurrence-free arrays of size n+1

w: This decomposition is the standard way to tame wildcard patterns: fix the middle anchor and pull the outer parts inward greedily. The empty-part identities (latestA[e]=e, earliestC[s]=s) are what make "**" → 0 and mixed cases work without special-casing. Pitfall: using naive find loops can degrade to O(n·|part|) on periodic inputs like "aaaa…". Follow-up: extend to k stars (fix k−1 anchors) or return the substring itself.
